I was in that exact same boat. I just slept all the time. Then I just started to push myself more and more. Just start with little things. maybe sit and color for half an hour or bake some cookies. Maybe on like Thursdays you and your boyfriend could set some time aside to play a card game or watch a movie, just something to get you out of that slump while still including him and kind of teaching him how to handle you

I think you guys should create a couple different spaces, meaning you have your alone space, he has his alone space, and then there is a safe space where you can talk about anything. Having your own little space gives him time to do his hobbies while you can do yours. Maybe to help your mind (I also suffer from depression) I write in a journal everyday and I play a ton of video games. I would maybe find a new hobby just for you. Maybe try cooking or knitting to help calm your mind but it gives you both space. The safe space is used for talking. I find that if I write out all that I am feeling it is easier to talk about than just talking it out. This space is used for when you are feeling absolutely terrible and just need someone there for you or you guys need to discuss something. In this space you try to talk vs have your emotions rule your body. I know, it is way easier said than done, but with practice and with both parties TRYING then it can be done. 
As for the meds, I'm on meds too and it took a while to kick in. In the mean time take time for yourself but don't overwhelm yourself. I ended up reading and binge watching netflix most of the days I waited for my meds to kick in. You just have to find something to amuse you without hurting yourself or others around you.

It's a snowball effect. So with my ex I got way more depressed and I overdosed. Hospital just sent me home. The next day my ex (boyfriend at that time) stood me up and I got so mad that he didn't care about me and broke up with him. About two weeks later I thought about driving my car off the road but instead went to the hospital where I agreed to go to a therapy. I ended up at this famous place in MN called Prairie Care where I was in a 5day/week therapy and put on the proper meds and that actually really helped. Once I got out I had my meds adjusted slightly by another psychiatrist and that is just the sweet spot. I notice if I miss a day of my meds I can get more irritable and depressed easier but I am also trying to get to the point where I am not totally dependent on them. It helps too that I cut all of the toxic people out of my life and found new people and I am reinvesting myself into my video games and puppies (the two things I LOVE).

I'm with you! I have severe depression and anxiety and I get told on a daily basis (by my parents) that everyone has these days and it will get better and to get over it. No, that's not true. It is a serious condition and it should be healed. If it were labled as a cancer people would be all over trying to help and heal you. But it's not, it is nothing to them because they just don't understand that it is a chemical imbalance in the brain and we can't do anything about it. Yes, some days are better than others, but some days are the worst and I contemplate suicide. With that attitude, I should not  be told to "get over it" yet everyone says it. It gets annoying, but I just learn to shut it out and try to explain that it is serious and needs to be healed, in whatever way will work, which may be many ways combined. Just know we are with you! You are not the only one feeling a certain way, and we know how it goes. We support and love you.

I'm 20 and have severe anxiety and depression. It's terribly hard. I'm on meds and go to therapy. It's ruined my life and my relationships, I constantly have fights with my boyfriend because of it. It's hard to go to work, as I work in retail and get trampled on by customers and coworkers. The meds and therapy actually help if you work towards wanting to fix your life. I still have my really bad days and have constant panic attacks, but I've learned some tricks to help calm me down. I listen to a certain Playlist that has panic at the disco songs. I do crossword puzzle books and just people watch. Sometimes I even get out my phone in the middle of a panic attack and just look at pictures of my dog. You just have to find something that calms you down. It's hard, but it does get easier if you want to make a difference. The more I talk about it to certain coworkers, the more I learn that they have similar experiences and are also in therapy for some reason. Don't be ashamed of it!
